name: mare

attributes.attribute: a mythological animal of special importance as the female horse
the continental horse goddess pictured riding a mare or surrounded by fillies
the Irish goddess who raced horses while pregnant, as though she were a mare
the Welsh goddess who rode a magical mare
the central sacred hill of Ireland with a rampart and ditch read as a horse temple
the 360-foot chalk horse carved into the Berkshire downs in 50 B.C.E.

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The mare was a mythological animal. Although horses held significance to the Celts, the female horse received special importance. The continental horse goddess Epona was pictured riding on a mare or surrounded by fillies. The Irish goddess Macha raced horses while pregnant, as though she were a mare herself. The Welsh goddess Rhiannon rode on a magical mare. At Uisneach, the central sacred hill of Ireland, a rampart and ditch have been interpreted as a horse temple. Beneath the outer ring were found tunnels in the shape of a stallion pursuing a mare. The sacred horse lived on in the folk belief in the true mare, the seventh consecutive filly. The most famous horse monument of Britain, the White Horse of Uffington, was dated to the Celtic era. The flowing white chalk figure was first carved into its hillside on the Berkshire downs in 50 B.C.E.

okr.objective: Document the mare, the mythological female horse of the Celts and its horse goddesses.
